edits.old: For Atlas, resolver deployment is conditional on DNS requirements, not an established universal prerequisite. This is a synthesis: Azure documents hybrid forwarding, while Atlas documents endpoint-specific connection strings resolving to private interface IPs. DNS success alone does not establish database connectivity. (medium confidence)
edits.new: Azure DNS Private Resolver enables DNS resolution between Azure virtual networks and on-premises environments, while Atlas documents that the hostname in a private endpoint-aware connection string is a DNS A record that resolves to the private IP address of the private endpoint's network interface (Azure Private Link). Whether a resolver is needed therefore depends on how the client's DNS can resolve that name (for example, on-premises clients need a forwarder path into Azure). Sources: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/dns/dns-private-resolver-overview ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/security-private-endpoint.md

evidence.quote: Azure DNS Private Resolver now provides a fully managed recursive resolution and conditional forwarding service for Azure virtual networks.
The inbound endpoint receives DNS queries that ingress to Azure.
The resolver's outbound endpoint processes DNS queries based on a DNS forwarding ruleset that you configure.
An outbound endpoint enables conditional forwarding name resolution from Azure to on-premises, other cloud providers, or external DNS servers.
